evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'Well, I'd love to get you all squared away here' and outlines the plan ('we'll kind of walk through piece by piece and then you'll be able to just give me the big pieces of furniture...and then I'll be able to kind of get your...get you squared away and tell you what that rate would look like') but does not use the exact time-boxed framing ('10 to 15 minutes') or wait explicitly for a yes before proceeding.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Pam Davis), moving day (October 26th), route (Fort Worth to Grandberry), size (1400 sq ft) — all confirmed: 'Let me confirm the first address which is the 7101. Cuban Boulevard and that's in Fort Worth and that's a one story house. Approximately 1400 square feet, is that correct?'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing has already started. Rep begins logistics questions ('Now that one car garage, can you fit your car in there or is it full of stuff?') before asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' This question is never explicitly asked in recognizable form.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep goes deep on multiple concerns: (1) Garage storage system — 'Okay, and that's not, it's not mounted on the wall. It's just in the garage, if I heard you correctly?' and follows up to clarify; (2) Packing uncertainty — rep asks multiple follow-ups about whether customer will pack or needs help, exploring the garage situation multiple times; (3) Damage concerns from prior move — customer raises this unprompted and rep responds with reassurance about trained employees.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep partially reflects back: 'So I know you had pack and checked here and then I did hear you say that you'll probably get your sister to come and you all will probably get everything packed up. Did I hear that correctly?' — this is a partial reflection on packing plans but does not comprehensively reflect all of the customer's concerns (garage storage system, damage worries, uncertainty about scope).
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (house), stories (one story), rooms (implied 2–3 bedroom, 1 bathroom), walking distance (not asked), garage (one car, full of stuff), special considerations (garage storage system not being moved, garage tools/equipment, donations pickup, donated furniture). Nearly all seven categories covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Yes: 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' (implied in discussion: 'Okay, generally if we're doing anything above a partial pack...'). Explicit offer framed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: No. Rep never asks 'A typical box count for a home your size is ________, do you have anything like china or a book collection that might put you over a typical count?' Customer volunteers 'I can't really count boxes Shany cause I don't really have boxes done' but rep does not follow up with the box-count / overflow check script.

top_strength: Chauntelle expertly recognized a ≥1,800 sq ft move scenario and cleanly routed the call to a virtual walkthrough (Section 1 compliance), then thoroughly gathered logistics details and explored the customer's primary concerns (garage uncertainty, prior damage experience) through genuine follow-up questions that built trust before pricing.
coaching_note: Ask 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to on this call?' earlier — before logistics probing starts — so that Section 2's agenda-setting happens first, not partway through the call.
